JobState.description:
Workflow state for a [`MaintenanceJob`].

PHASE-0A.md §16 lists the canonical 18-state workflow, but `CandidateAssembly` appears twice — likely a spec typo. We replace the **second** occurrence with `SourceRevision`, producing 19 distinct variants:

```text EventDetected, Intake, SourceReview, CandidateAssembly, SourceRevision, SourceIntegrity, BuildValidation, PackageQaValidation, FunctionalValidation, UpgradeValidation, ReleaseReview, FinalValidation, ReadyForApproval, Approved, PublicationPending, Published, HumanReviewRequired, InfrastructureBlocked, Cancelled ```

`SourceRevision` is a manual source-tweak window between the initial candidate build and the source-integrity check; an operator may edit packaging files there without invalidating the state machine. The state machine in 0A.3 will encode the rules for entering and leaving this state.

oneOf.description: Initial state: a maintenance event has been detected upstream.
Triaging the event: assigning it to a job and target package.
Reviewing upstream source state (tags, commits, security feeds).
Producing the initial source candidate and packaging inputs.
Manual source-tweak window between initial build and integrity check.
Verifying the source tree (checksums, signatures, provenance).
Running distribution package QA (Lintian / rpmlint) gates.
Running upgrade-test gates on existing installs.
Reviewing the assembled release metadata (changelog, notes).
All gates passed; awaiting explicit human approval.
Human approval recorded; cleared to publish.
Success terminal: artifacts are in the canonical repos.
Exceptional: paused for human review (gate ambiguity, risk).
Exceptional: paused by infrastructure failure (worker / network).
Terminal: cancelled by operator or policy.

resumed_to.description: The state the job was returned to, read back from the projection rather than echoed from the command's side-effect strings — the same reasoning `check.run` follows when it reports its outcome.
